@graph.headline: AI Agent Memory: From Chat History to Persistent Systems
@graph.description: How to give AI agents memory that persists across sessions — CLAUDE.md, mem0, ChromaDB, and the architecture that makes agents smarter over time.
@graph.keywords: ai agent memory, persistent memory ai, claude code memory, mem0 mcp, ai agent context
@graph.abstract: Persistent memory is the defining capability of production AI agents. By combining short-term working context, semantic vector retrieval, and structured JSON entity graphs, agents maintain coherence and institutional knowledge across sessions.

mainEntity.name: What are the three layers of AI agent memory?

acceptedAnswer.text: Immediate working context (active prompt window), episodic memory (vector retrieval of past conversations), and semantic memory (structured knowledge graphs).

mainEntity.name: How do you prevent memory bloat in long-running agents?

acceptedAnswer.text: Through periodic summarization, memory compaction routines, and relevance score thresholds during retrieval.

mainEntity.name: What database technologies power agent memory?

acceptedAnswer.text: Vector databases like Qdrant and pgvector combined with relational or key-value stores like SQLite and DynamoDB.

mainEntity.name: How does MCP standardize memory access?

acceptedAnswer.text: Via dedicated memory MCP servers that expose standard tools for creating, reading, updating, and querying relation graphs.

mainEntity.name: How do agents resolve conflicting memories?

acceptedAnswer.text: By applying timestamp precedence and source validation trust scores to prioritize recent and higher-authority data.
